name: New Year's Day
description: Marks the first day of the civil calendar year under the old-world dating system. The date served as a formal reset point for records, contracts, inventories, and personal resolutions.

name: Anchorage Liberation Day
description: Marks the United States recapture of Anchorage during the final stage of the Sino-American War. Pre-war records treated the victory as proof of restored military initiative after more than a decade of Alaskan fighting.

name: MLK Jr. Birthday
description: Honors Martin Luther King Jr., a pre-war civil rights leader born on January 15, 1929. The date is associated with nonviolent protest and the expansion of federal civil rights protections.

name: Valentine's Day
description: A pre-war social holiday centered on courtship, affection, and reciprocal gift exchange. Surviving customs emphasize cards, sweets, flowers, meals, and other tokens of attachment.

name: Washington's Birthday
description: Honors George Washington, the first president of the United States and a central figure in old-world civic mythology. Later usage often broadened the date into a general observance of the presidency.

name: Leap Year Hype
description: Marks the extra calendar day inserted during leap years to keep civil time aligned with the solar year. Its rarity made most associated customs informal, temporary, or locally invented.

name: St. Patrick's Day
description: An Irish religious and cultural feast day that became a broad public celebration in many pre-war American cities. Surviving material links the date to Irish identity, parades, music, alcohol, and the color green.

name: April Fools' Day
description: A customary day for jokes, false reports, and minor social deception. Historical records indicate reduced reliability of public claims on this date.

name: Indulgence Day
description: An informal observance associated with recreational chem use, food, rest, and tolerated vice. Legal status and medical risk varied by settlement, supply, and local authority.

name: Earth Day
description: A pre-war environmental observance dedicated to land, water, air, and ecological stewardship. Post-war usage frames the date through reclamation, radiation survey, and scientific efforts.

name: Workers' Day
description: An international observance recognizing workers, unions, strikes, and collective bargaining. Not recognized in pre-war America due to its inherent association with socialistic values and the Chinese party.

name: Cinco de Mayo
description: Marks Mexico's 1862 victory over French forces at the Battle of Puebla. In the pre-war United States, the date often broadened into a celebration of Mexican culture and community identity.

name: Mother's Day
description: A family observance honoring mothers and maternal figures. Pre-war customs emphasized cards, flowers, meals, and recognition of domestic care.

name: Juneteenth
description: Commemorates the June 19, 1865 announcement of emancipation in Texas after the American Civil War. The date represents freedom, delayed justice, and the survival of memory beyond official proclamation.

name: Father's Day
description: A family observance honoring fathers and paternal figures. Pre-war customs emphasized cards, meals, practical gifts, and recognition of domestic care.

name: Independence Day
description: Marks the adoption of the United States Declaration of Independence in 1776. Pre-war usage joined civic ceremony, military display, and fireworks. Post-war, it connects with efforts of national continuity.

name: Last Peace Day
description: Marks the formal dissolution of the United Nations on July 26, 2052, during the opening phase of the Resource Wars. The date represents the failure of old-world collective security before the Sino-American War.

name: Labor Day
description: A United States labor observance from the early September civil calendar recognizing workers and the labor movement. Pre-war usage shifted the date toward civic rest, travel, retail activity, and the symbolic end of summer.

name: Enclave Remembrance Day
description: A disputed post-war memorial date attributed to Enclave survivors, sympathizers, or local records. Where retained, it frames Enclave defeats as losses of governmental continuity rather than factional collapse.

name: The Jubilee
description: A local commemorative date marking the founding of a revered establishment of unclear but persistent cultural significance. Surviving references associate the event with patronage and efficient use of interior space.

name: Founder's Vigil
description: Marks Roger Maxson's secession from the United States at Mariposa Military Base, later treated as the Brotherhood of Steel's ideological origin. The date represents duty, diligence, and independence.

name: Great War Anniversary
description: Marks October 23, 2077, the day the old world ended in total nuclear annihilation, both the peak and the end of the Sino-American War. The date is associated with vault activation, civil defense, and mass casualty remembrance.

name: Reclamation Day
description: Commemorates the opening of Vault 76 on October 23, 2102, twenty-five years after the Great War. In Vault-Tec records, the date marks the transition from sealed preservation to authorized surface reclamation.

name: Halloween
description: A pre-war seasonal holiday involving costumes, masks, sweets, and theatrical fear. The Great War left many decorations in place, giving the date added scavenger and memorial significance.

name: Day of the Dead
description: A Mexican remembrance tradition honoring deceased family members and ancestors. Surviving accounts emphasize offerings, marigolds, food, candles, altars, and continued memory rather than simple mourning.

name: Veterans Day
description: Honors military veterans and their service under the United States flag. Post-war use depends on whether the date is treated as remembrance, recruitment, or factional legitimacy.

name: Christmas Eve
description: The evening before Christmas, associated with family gatherings, travel, preparation, and religious services. Pre-war households also used the date for meal preparation, gift placement, and final domestic ceremony.

name: Christmas Day
description: A winter holiday with Christian origins and broad pre-war cultural adoption. Typical customs included gifts, meals, music, decorated trees, charitable gestures, and domestic peace rhetoric.

name: New Year's Eve
description: The final night of the civil calendar year, associated with countdowns, gatherings, music, and drinking. Settlements with functioning clocks or civic records may use the date for year-end inventories and watch changes.
